pinnedFiles.reason: The Gherkin for this order's AC3:ui and AC4:ui covers -- business-language traceability for 'seeded expeditions drawn where seeded' and 'a signed-in adventurer's own expedition drawn with the seeded ones, never another adventurer's'. draw-line.feature and save-expedition.feature in the same directory belong to the next two orders and are excluded.
The Gherkin for this order's AC5 cover -- flying to Tidewrack Shoals from the far side brings it to the near side. Single scenario, directly maps to the claim's second acceptance criterion.

The file this order extends. Already draws reagent-site point entities tagged with saturdayMetadata {id, name, kind:'site'} and sets window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ -- expeditions must follow the identical per-entity tagging pattern with kind:'expedition', and the camera fly-to must use viewer.camera.flyTo the same way buildViewer() already uses camera.setView. Note for the analyst: Cesium's PolylineGraphics defaults to a straight Cartesian3 chord, not a surface-following path -- rendering 'geodesic' per the spec's settled gate needs arcType: Cesium.ArcType.GEODESIC (or equivalent) against this view's custom 6,000km-sphere ellipsoid, not Earth's default.
The exact client pattern (type, runtime API_BASE resolution, fetch-with-timeout, throw-on-!ok) a new src/api/expeditions.ts module should mirror for fetchExpeditions().

Shows the only existing pattern in this app for attaching the Authorization header from localStorage('dnd_auth_token') to a GET. GET /api/expeditions is unauthenticated-tolerant but visibility-sensitive (shop's seeded expeditions always; the caller's own only with a valid token) -- the new expeditions client needs this same optional-auth-header shape, not orders.ts's full getAuthHeaders Content-Type variant verbatim.

Defines the seam contract already in production use: getEntities() reads entity.polyline.positions as a {line: GeoPoint[]} geometry when saturdayMetadata is present (no new fixture code needed for expedition lines), and flyTo(lat,lng,heightMeters) already drives viewer.camera.flyTo + waitForSettled -- this is the exact mechanism AC5's 'fly to a site' must trigger from the production view, and the exact mechanism the new test will assert against. Read before designing either the view change or its test.
Pure distance()/lineLength() helpers, radius-parameterized (never Earth's) -- what the new test asserts 'both ends within 1 km of stored ends' with, matching reagent-map-globe's precedent test.

The seed fixture: 3 shop-owned expeditions (AC3) plus Elara's and Borin's own (AC4), each {id, name, owner, from:{lat,lng}, to:{lat,lng}, savedAt}. GET /api/expeditions (apps/mock-api/server.js, not in scope.paths, not pinned) filters this list server-side by owner==='shop' or the session's own id -- the frontend only needs to render whatever the endpoint returns and attach the Authorization header when signed in; no client-side filtering logic is needed or correct to add.

Already-established Expedition/GeoPoint types ({id, name?, owner, from, to}) and visibleExpeditions()/saveExpedition() methods, used by the existing (out-of-scope, already-shipped) API-level spec reagent-map-api.spec.ts. The new src/api/expeditions.ts client's Expedition type should match this shape so UI and API-test code agree on the same domain object.

House style for the sibling spec this order adds: @orieken/saturday-playwright-cesium's test/cesium fixture import, data-testid='reagent-site-list' locator pattern, and the existing 'Frostcap Hollow and Tidewrack Shoals stay single entities after flying to each' test already exercises cesium.flyTo() against the production view's seam -- the new fly-to-site test is a close sibling of this one, not a new pattern.
